long_biography.plain_text:
Acquiring Manchester City in 2008 gave Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan the foundation for City Football Group. The organisation developed an international network of football clubs under a majority stake held through his wholly owned Newton Investment and Development. The resulting group brought clubs across several continents under a common ownership and operating organisation.

Mansour also serves as UAE Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Presidential Court. His responsibilities combine senior federal and court work with leadership of major investment institutions. He chairs both the Emirates Investment Authority and Mubadala Investment Company.

Sports is selected because CFG is the largest substantial private holding attributable specifically and transparently to Sheikh Mansour in the reviewed evidence. Broader Al Nahyan family holdings are opaque and were not assigned to him individually.
EIA and Mubadala are explicitly treated as sovereign or government-owned institutions. His chairmanships establish public stewardship, not personal ownership of their portfolios.
No dedicated personal Forbes profile was found. Current Forbes team pages name him as owner, but they are not substitutes for a person profile and are not proposed as a Forbes social record.

A current Aletihad report independently attributes and embeds the @hhmansour Instagram account, so it is proposed alongside the corroborated X account. A name-matched LinkedIn profile and possible personal websites lacked equivalent confirmation and were rejected.
No second nationality was evidenced, so the blank secondary-nationality field remains unfilled.

Blank suffix, secondary residence, death, age, internal-note and unknown-name fields were treated as optional, inapplicable or system fields rather than enrichment targets.
